## Design

### 2026-10-01 — Today, I worked on my Smart Workshop Sensor project. The goal of the project is to build a small and useful device that can measure and display different environmental values in a workshop, garage, or

**5h**

Today, I worked on my Smart Workshop Sensor project. The goal of the project is to build a small and useful device that can measure and display different environmental values in a workshop, garage, or room.

First, I planned the main features of the project and decided which components I would need. The main components are an ESP32 microcontroller, a BME280 sensor, an OLED display, and a BH1750 light sensor. I also planned to use buttons and LEDs to create a simple user interface and status system.

After planning the hardware, I created a complete parts list and checked the estimated costs. One important requirement is that the complete project should cost no more than 65 US dollars. I therefore focused on affordable components while still trying to keep the project reliable and useful.

I also planned the software structure for the ESP32. I want to program it using C++ with PlatformIO in Visual Studio Code. The device should show temperature, humidity, air pressure, and light intensity on the OLED display.

Finally, I started planning the 3D-printed enclosure. It should be compact, clean, and practical, with openings for the sensors and space for the display, buttons, and LEDs.

Overall, today I focused mainly on planning, researching components, and designing the basic concept of the project.

### 2026-10-01 — ![Intelligenter Arbeitsplatz mit Sensordashboard](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5KJCSapCjUMgPm1B9K1fQItdfMNbc5O0/e055cebc86d6e689df1c9d0528f403f516c08bac6c075513af2e

**2h**

![Intelligenter Arbeitsplatz mit Sensordashboard](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/5KJCSapCjUMgPm1B9K1fQItdfMNbc5O0/e055cebc86d6e689df1c9d0528f403f516c08bac6c075513af2ec4cd5c08eb13.png)
The Smart Workspace Station is a compact smart device designed to sit directly on a desk. Its housing contains several environmental sensors, a small computer, a touchscreen display, wireless connectivity, and a rechargeable battery or power connection.

Inside the station are multiple sensors that continuously monitor the environment. A temperature sensor measures the current room temperature, while a humidity sensor monitors the amount of moisture in the air. A barometric pressure sensor measures atmospheric pressure, and a light sensor detects the brightness around the workspace. These sensors work together to create a detailed picture of the user's working environment.

The front of the device contains a touchscreen with a simple and modern user interface. The main dashboard shows all measurements in real time using clear icons, numbers, and colored indicators. Users can switch between different menus to view statistics, sensor history, settings, and notifications.

One of the coolest features is the smartphone app. The station can connect to the phone via Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, allowing users to see their workspace data remotely. The app can display graphs, save historical measurements, send alerts, and show changes over time.

The station could also include smart notifications. For example, it could warn the user when the room becomes too warm, too humid, too dark, or when another measured value changes significantly.

With its compact design, environmental sensors, touchscreen, wireless connection, and mobile app, the Smart Workspace Station combines useful technology in one small device.
